source: Traced by hand and by color from USGS NAIP aerial photos (public domain), to fill in what OpenStreetMap doesn't have yet.

unsure.all: Hole order and which holes belong to South rather than West are my best guess beyond hole 5: the club's sites give no hole map and the two courses share the grounds.
unsure.1: Fairly sure: long tee beside the south clubhouse and practice green, about 525 yards south to a green with a front-left bunker and water/houses on the left, as the club describes hole 1.
unsure.2: Fairly sure: par 3 with the pond and bunker on the left and the road (out of bounds) on the right, as described.
unsure.3: Fairly sure: north along the road with water left, two bunkers front-right, as described.
unsure.4: Tee not clearly visible; placed south-east of the 3rd green. Green has front-left and front-right bunkers as described.
unsure.5: Par 5 north to a green with water and a bunker short; tee placed at the south end of the fairway.
unsure.7: Par 3 green found; tee not visible, placed on the strip east of it, so it measures short.
unsure.13: Small green on a point in a lake; tee not visible, placed north-east of it.
unsure.15: Re-traced as a par 5: the fairway of the old line continues south and turns east along the road under the lake, so the tee is placed on that south strip just west of the 12th green; no tee pads visible there, so the tee position is a guess from the card length. Small tee pads west of the lake near this green may belong to a short hole of another course
unsure.17: Par 3 along the road; tee not clearly visible.
unsure.18: Taken as 18 because it finishes beside the south clubhouse; tee placed at the south end of the fairway.
unsure.12: Re-traced: the old line crossed a lake. The photo shows a fairway running south down the east side of the wide west fairway, through the gap between two lakes, to the green beside the main road. Tee not visible, placed just east of the tree clump at the north end; this shares the wide fairway with hole 10 (opposite way), so which hole is 12 is still a guess
unsure.16: Tee moved to the darker tee pad on the north shore of the big lake, just west of the gap between the two lakes, at the south end of the fairway that runs north to the green on the lake edge; it now measures within the card. A second darker pad by the cart path in the gap itself may be a further-back tee, but it sits on hole 12's line through the gap, so I left it. The long walk from this green to the 17th tee is left as it is: the green is in the far north-west corner and 17 starts by the south road, so it comes from the back-nine hole order, which is still a guess
unsure.14: Re-traced: tee moved off the tree line to the grass at the lake's north-west tip, a short walk from the 13th green; line follows the fairway down the west side of the lake to the green. Tee pads not clearly visible
